title: gui_cancel_drag() causes hard game crash when drag preview Control is freed
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in: - v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] - v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1] - v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6] ### System information Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8180) - AMD Ryzen 7 5700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads) - 31.88 GiB memory ### Issue description Issue description When using Drag & Drop with `Control` nodes, calling `Viewport.gui_cancel_drag()` can cause a **hard game crash** under specific lifecycle conditions involving the drag preview. The crash occurs when a `Control` node is used as a drag preview via `set_drag_preview()`, and this preview belongs to a subtree that gets freed (`queue_free()` is called on one of its parents). When the preview `Control` exits the scene tree (`_exit_tree()` is called), and **after that** `get_viewport().gui_cancel_drag()` is called from another node, the game crashes immediately without any error message or crash report — the game simply closes. ### Expected behavior Calling `gui_cancel_drag()` should safely cancel the current drag operation, even if the drag preview `Control` has already exited the scene tree or been freed. At worst, the function should fail gracefully or do nothing, but it should never crash the game. From an API and gameplay-logic perspective, it makes sense for the node that started the drag operation to be able to cancel it while it is being destroyed. For example, in an inventory system with multiple draggable slots, a slot may not know *when* the inventory UI will be closed, but it **does know** that if it is being freed, any active drag operation it started must be cancelled. Actual behavior The game crashes instantly if `gui_cancel_drag()` (or `get_viewport().gui_cancel_drag()`) is called **after** the drag preview `Control` has exited the scene tree (or after its own `_exit_tree()` has already run) due to `queue_free()` on one of its parents. Additional notes - If `gui_cancel_drag()` is called **before** the drag preview’s `_exit_tree()` is triggered, everything works correctly and no crash occurs. - In practice, this makes the issue difficult to work around, because the drag preview is automatically reparented by the engine when the drag starts, making it hard to guarantee that `gui_cancel_drag()` is always called early enough. --- In the first image, if the node marked with a **red X** calls `queue_free()`, and one of the **yellow nodes** calls `get_viewport().gui_cancel_drag()` inside its `_exit_tree()`, the game crashes due to the order in which `_exit_tree()` is executed. The `_exit_tree()` callbacks are called from the **deepest node to the highest parent**. In this case, the execution order is: - Preview - ColorRect2 - ColorRect - Control5 - Control4 - Node Because the drag preview’s `_exit_tree()` runs before `gui_cancel_drag()` is called, cancelling the drag afterward results in a crash. --- ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2edb7bfe-b306-4a9f-998a-46c9ad5f2823) In the second image, if `get_viewport().gui_cancel_drag()` is called from one of the nodes marked with a **green X**, the crash does **not** occur. This is because `gui_cancel_drag()` is executed in the `_exit_tree()` of a node that runs **before** the drag preview’s `_exit_tree()`, meaning the drag operation is cancelled while the preview is still valid. --- ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the provided minimal reproduction project. 2. Run any of the test scenes listed below. 3. Start a drag operation by dragging the `ColorRect`. 4. Open the **Remote** scene tree to observe where the drag preview node is reparented. 5. Check the output/logs, which also print the parent node of the drag preview. 6. In scenes **3, 4, 5, and 5_2**, after starting the drag operation, press **Enter** to trigger `queue_free()` and observe the behavior. ## Minimal reproduction project (MRP) **Godot version:** v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] This project contains multiple small test scenes, each demonstrating a specific Drag & Drop scenario related to the crash. ### Scene 1 Demonstrates where the drag preview is inserted in the scene tree. The preview follows the logic of walking up the tree starting from the node that initiated the drag, stopping when a parent is no longer a `CanvasItem`. ### Scene 2 Similar to Scene 1, but with a `Node` placed between `Control` nodes, showing how a non-`CanvasItem` affects preview placement. ### Scene 3 Shows that calling `queue_free()` and `get_viewport().gui_cancel_drag()` from the **same node** inside `_exit_tree()` works correctly and cancels the drag without crashing. ### Scene 4 Same purpose as Scene 3, reinforcing that cancelling the drag from the node being freed behaves correctly. ### Scene 5 Demonstrates that calling `get_viewport().gui_cancel_drag()` **before** the drag preview’s `_exit_tree()` and before the `_exit_tree()` of the node that called `queue_free()` works correctly. ### Scene 5_2 Demonstrates the **actual crash**. If `get_viewport().gui_cancel_drag()` is called **after** the drag preview’s `_exit_tree()` has already been executed, the game crashes immediately. godot verson: v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439] [bug_drag_drop_godot_4_6_stable.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24919583/bug_drag_drop_godot_4_6_stable.zip)
